title: Container Bookings: How Goodwill Conditions on Roll Fees Combine
content:
A Container Bookings goodwill request on a customer roll fee ends in one of two ways, a full waiver or none; this page states how the conditions governing it combine and what amount a granted waiver carries.

## Rule

A waiver is written only when every condition of the goodwill basis for customer roll fees is met at the same time. That basis does not replace the general goodwill rules of Container Bookings; it adds to them. A customer roll fee entry that satisfies every general condition but fails one of the added ones, such as the completeness of the change account, the requirement of a positive amount or the contract condition, receives no waiver. The general rules' yearly quota and their rule that an entry is waived at most once keep their full force in deciding whether any waiver can be written.

When all conditions hold, the waiver amount is the amount of the fee entry addressed, rounded to two decimal places. If even one condition fails, nothing is written: the fee entry keeps its full amount as a debt, and cutting it down lies outside the desk's powers.

## Truth table (hypothetical)

| Added conditions all met | General conditions all met | Waiver |
|---|---|---|
| yes | yes | written for the entry's full amount |
| yes | no | none |
| no | yes | none |
| no | no | none |

## Worked example (hypothetical)

A customer roll fee entry of 180.00 meets every condition: the waiver is 180.00, cancelling the entry entirely. Had one condition failed, the waiver would be nil and the 180.00 would stay payable; the desk could not settle on, say, 90.00 instead. The amounts are invented.
